question: Ms. Carroll promised that anyone who got all the multiple choice questions right on the upcoming exam would receive an A on the exam. Which one of these statements necessarily follows logically?
solution:
Consider what the promise tells us about a student who does not receive an A. If Lewis had answered every multiple choice question correctly, the promise would guarantee him an A. Therefore, if he did not receive an A, he must have gotten at least one multiple choice question wrong. This is the contrapositive of the promise.

Here, “not all correct” means “at least one wrong,” not “all wrong.” The promise also allows students who miss questions to receive an A.

The necessary conclusion is statement \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
